title: Efficiency Training
texts: Boulder repeats with an emphasis on movement optimization

Choose a boulder that is at your typical flash grade.  Climb the boulder once, focusing on hip engagement and footwork.  Isolate one move on the problem that you can do more efficiently and focus on improving that move on your next attempt.  If you have trouble identifying moves to improve, observe other climbers attempting the problem or ask for input from more experienced climbers.  Filming yourself and reviewing the footage between attempts is also a great way to identify potential improvements.  Rest for 3-5 minutes between each attempt and complete a total of 3 repetitions on each boulder.

After completing the first boulder, rest for 5 minutes before completing the process on 3 more boulders.  In total, you will climb 4 boulders, 3 times each, for a total of 12 problems.
